Headteacher's welcome
Hello and welcome to Trafalgar Schools Federation
We are a community school in Twickenham, South West London, in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, and are federation of Infant and Junior School. The Trafalgar Federation was set up to provide a smooth and successful journey for our children through their primary education.
We are committed to both pupil achievement and pupil development through our values of Believe, Inspire, Achieve. This means that through the wide experiences that we offer, we aim to challenge our children to achieve academically while also developing their confidence, self-esteem and a positive attitude towards learning.
We hope that you will find our website informative and helpful. Whether you are a prospective parent, somebody who might be interested in working at our school, or are already part of our school community, we hope that there is something here for you.
We are confident that you will see that Trafalgar is a vibrant, inclusive and happy place to be. We are proud of our children, our staff and the provision we offer. If you don’t already know us and would like to visit, please contact our school office to make an appointment.

Trips, Visits and Curriculum Experiences
At Trafalgar Schools' we plan a wide range of visits, trips and curriculum experiences that support and enrich our children's learning across all subject areas and Key Stages. Last year these included:
Reception children welcoming a farm to our Meadway site for the day.
Year 1 children visiting London Zoo and Y2 children visiting Strawberry Hill House and The Stockyard at Bushy Park.
Year 3 visiting a local church and taking part in a Stone Age workshop and Year 4 visiting a Gurdwara and taking part in a Roman workshop.
Year 5 visiting the Natural History Museum and Twickenham Apiary and Year 6 visiting Kew National Archives and a Hindu Mandir. Year 5 and 6 also went on residential trips to Juniper Hall and Kingswood.

Safeguarding
Trafalgar Schools’ Federation (TSF) is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
TSF has a duty to ensure that all parents understand our responsibility to safeguard the wellbeing of all pupils and that this responsibility requires us to have Safeguarding including child protection procedures including online safety. As part of these procedures the school can make a direct referral to the statutory child welfare agencies including the Police and/or Social Services without involving the parents if they have concerns about the safety of any child.
Mrs. Keefe (Headteacher) is the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) Mrs. Burton (Deputy Headteacher), and Mrs. Brown and Mrs. Gale (SenCos ) are the Deputy DSLs. Mr. Hutchins (Governor) is the Nominated Governor for Safeguarding.
If you have any concerns about the welfare of children in our school please share those concerns with us. Please leave a message with the school office or telephone the main school number on 020 8894 5729.
Out of Hours/School Holidays
If you want to speak to someone about a safeguarding concern out of school hours or during the holidays then please contact the Richmond Single Point of Access (SPA) using the contact details below:
Call 020 8547 5008 from 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday, or 020 8770 5000 out of hours.
Or call 999 if you think a child or young person is in immediate danger.
You can access the latest version of our Safeguarding Policy inc Child Protection from our Policies page

Pupil Leadership
At Trafalgar Schools' we encourage all our children to be involved in a range of activities, including taking on responsibilities and participating in the wider life of the school.
KS1
School Council
In September, we hold elections in each class. We all vote for a boy and a girl to become our class representatives for the School Council. We then meet regularly with Mrs Keefe and Mrs Burton to discuss issues which are important to our school.
Digital Leaders
Digital Leaders are trained to help pupils across the school understand, enjoy and use technology safely. They help Mrs Peach deliver online-safety assemblies, support children to log on and off and trial new apps, software and games.
T.I.G.E.Rs
The Trafalgar Infant Green Environmental Rangers (TIGERs) are nominated by class teachers in September. Ms. Hutchins holds regular meetings to discuss ways to make our school more environmentally friendly.
Musical Maestros
Musical Maestros are chosen for their love and enthusiasm for music. They help with music assemblies, choir rehearsals and performances and promoting music across the school both during lesson time and playtime.
Listening Friends
Listening Friends are trained and meet regularly to talk about how things are going. They take turns at playtime to help children deal with worries. If a child has a worry about something they can come to talk to a Listening Friend.
Reading Ambassadors
Reading Ambassadors help to look after their class reading areas, our shared reading areas and our library.
KS2
School Council
In September we hold elections in each class. Pupils vote for a boy and a girl to become class representatives for the School Council and a boy and a girl to act as Deputies. The School Council then meet regularly with Mrs Keefe and Mrs Burton to discuss issues which are important to our school. Our School Councillors for this academic year will be announced at assembly and published in the weekly newsletter.
Head Boy and Head Girl
Children in Y6 are invited to apply for the role. The chosen candidates and deputies are announced in the weekly newsletter.
Anti-Bullying Ambassadors
A group of Y5 and Y6 children who have been trained to support other children on the playground. We are currently working towards an accreditation from the Diana Foundation.
Reading Ambassadors
Our keen readers in Y6 help promote a love of reading across the school.

Helping the lower school with clubs and events.

Behaviour and our Golden Rules
We believe in having high expectations of children’s attitudes towards their learning and their behaviour.
Behaviour
Our Positive Relationships and Behaviour Policy inc. anti-bullying can be found on our Policies Page:Policies page We use our Golden Rules to reinforce our aims in encouraging positive behaviour, which are:
The Golden Rules
Anti-Bullying
At Trafalgar we have a zero-tolerance policy of bullying of any kind. We actively promote values or respect and equality and celebrate diversity across the school. This allows our pupils to become responsible citizens and appreciate modern society when they leave our school.
We define bullying as unkind behaviour from one child to another that is on purpose and on-going. It can happen in person or online. We discuss how bullying typically involves a power balance which can be physical, verbal or social (e.g. excluding someone and encouraging others to do the same. Children are taught that if they experience behaviour the don’t like from others they say “Stop it. I don’t like it”. They then walk away and tell a trusted adult. The children are regularly encouraged to about think who their trusted adult is. We also encourage children to be ‘up standers’ rather than ‘bystanders’.
To encourage positive behaviour, KS2 have Anti-Bullying Ambassadors who are on duty in the playground at lunchtime and easily identifiable. These children are introduced in assembly at the start of the school year and their role is support happy playtimes for all and KS1 have Listening Friends.

Welcome from TSF Governing Body
Trafalgar Infant & Junior Schools are community schools belonging to Trafalgar Schools’ Federation (TSF).
Greetings from the Governing Body of Trafalgar Schools Federation. We are proud to play our part in supporting two vibrant schools where every child is valued, encouraged, and given the best chance to succeed.
Our Governing Body is made up of volunteers from a variety of backgrounds and professions, bringing together different skills and perspectives. Some of us are parents or staff with the Federation, while others have no direct connection but share a commitment to education and making a positive difference for our pupils and our community.
As governors, our role is not to run the day-to-day life of the school(s), that is the responsibility of the Headteacher and the Senior Leadership Team. We work alongside them to provide strategic direction, ensure accountability and to monitor and evaluate performance.
Our responsibilities are wide-ranging and include; helping to shape education development plans, setting targets, reviewing performance, overseeing staff appointments, handling complaints, and making decisions about how the budget is spent.
How do we get involved?
Our Board and various governing committees meet every term but also visit the schools’ regularly to see learning and wellbeing in action and review first-hand how the schools’ vision is being brought to life.
We also set up Working Groups to address specific areas where necessary. Working together, we aim to uphold the values of the Schools’ Federation, celebrate successes, and continue to look for ways to improve so that every child can reach their full potential.
Our Chair of the Governing Body, Sophie Riley, finished at the end of summer term 2026 - we thank her for all her leadership and support - we will be electing a new Chair at the FGB in Autumn 2026.
Our Acting Chair of the Governing Body is Laura Jennings who will take on Co-Chair for 2026/27
If you wish to contact the governors, please email governors@trafalgarfederation.org.uk.
Are you our next Parent Governor?
We are holding elections for a new Parent Governor to join the Board from November 2026.
If you are interested please read through the process documentation and complete your nomination form. Deadline is 23rd October '26.
We look forward to hearing from you.
Our Committees
The three key roles of the Governing Body are; setting strategic direction, ensuring accountability, and monitoring and evaluating school performance. We meet as a Full Governing Body at least four times each year, but most of our work is carried out through our committees.
Each of these deals with a specific area of the schools’ organisation, planning and management. All have a responsibility to review Safeguarding within their committee remit.

Individual Needs & SEND
We recognise that all our children are individuals and therefore different. They have different needs and different contributions to make to the life of our school.
Helpful Information and Resources
download_for_offlineParent workshops information 18 09 26
Inclusion and Accessibility
Our Special Education Needs Co-ordinators (SenCo) advise on good practice in line with latest Government and local guidance and any changes are reflected in our Inclusion Policy, our TSF SEND Information Report and our Accessibility Strategy and Action Plan all of which can be found on our Policies page. Our Accessibility Action Plan is reviewed each term by our Governing Body. This enables us to consider any additional actions to increase access to the school and the curriculum by children with disabilities. Further information can also be found in our equality statement below.
Pupil Premium Grant
Our Pupil Premium Strategy outlines how we support families who are eligible for the Government’s Pupil Premium Grant. Documents supporting these initiatives can be found on our Polices page.
Equality
At Trafalgar Junior School we believe in equality of opportunity. We will follow the existing equality legislation (The Equality Act(2010)) that now extends protection from discrimination in nine areas: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion and belief, sex, sexual orientation. We will eliminate unlawful discrimination, advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations for children, staff, mothers, fathers, carers and all others who use the school facilities. Please see our Equalities Policy which is available from our Policies page.
We will meet diverse needs and advance equality by:
